new: to make (someone) embarrassed; me da vergüenza = I'm embarrassed
note: Story uses le daba vergüenza hablarlo = he was embarrassed to speak it; the old gloss suggests the thing is embarrassing, not the person.
On a bicycle these are panniers; 'saddlebags' suggests a horse.
In the story it is the spare inner tube for the flat tire.
Story: se secó los ojos = he dried his eyes.

new: bell (here: the school bell); also doorbell
note: Timbre is any bell/buzzer; 'school bell' only in context.
It is the small bell that rings when the shop door opens, not an electric doorbell (that's el timbre).
In the story Marta longs for the place and person she is leaving; 'homesickness' is too narrow and is listed first.

new: to let (someone) know, to tell in advance; also to warn
note: No quiso avisarle = she didn't want to tell him in advance; 'warn' first is misleading.
Correct in context, but learners should know the more frequent meaning 'bank' (b1-02 uses banco = bank).
